title: Scaling Up Memory Disaggregated Applications with SMART
problem: IOPS-bound memory disaggregated applications are limited by network bandwidth when performing concurrent fine-grained remote memory accesses, failing to scale beyond 32 cores.
motivation: Memory disaggregation with RDMA is becoming prevalent, but network scalability bottlenecks prevent applications from fully utilizing modern many-core processors.
method: When many cores simultaneously request data from remote memory, each request competes for limited network bandwidth, creating a bottleneck that prevents scaling beyond about 32 cores. SMART addresses this by bundling multiple memory requests into single network packets (request batching), overlapping the sending and receiving of data so the network stays constantly busy (pipelining), and timing when requests go out based on current network conditions (network-aware scheduling). These techniques multiply how many requests the same network can handle per second, enabling efficient operation with dozens of cores.
key_novelty: Batching and pipelining memory requests to match network bandwidth can overcome the bottleneck that prevents disaggregated memory systems from scaling across many cores.
contributions: Identifies and quantifies the network IOPS bottleneck in disaggregated memory systems
Proposes SMART architecture for improved concurrent remote access handling
Achieves scaling beyond 32-core limitation on many-core machines
Provides architectural insights for disaggregated memory system design
limitations: Not discussed in the provided abstract.
